sampling_model.design: Two independent fixed-size arms sample from \(K\) equal-probability covariate cells. The primary parameter is a pair of deterministic sign arrays in \(\mathcal T_K(r)\). The lower experiment is indexed by \(q\in\mathcal R_K^{\circ}(r)\) and mixes only over the legal shell \(|\rho_K-q|\le s_K\).
sampling_model.units: Within each arm, observations are independent. Conditional on a sampled cell, the outcome is Bernoulli with the cell probability \(p_{dj}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Arm membership is fixed by the two-sample design; treatment and control samples are independent and no unit appears in both arms.
sampling_model.overlap: Every cell has sampling probability \(1/K\) in each arm, while cross-arm overlap is governed by \(\lambda_K=n_0n_1/K\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The amplitudes \(a\) and \(b\) are known. The sign arrays are unrestricted apart from membership in \(\mathcal T_K(r)\); the procedure estimates their empirical cross-arm correlation only through collision marks. Continuous transfer uses \(U_{di}\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) and is compared with the discrete design only after the measurable pushforward \(\mathsf Q_K\).

body.tldr: For binary outcomes on a growing uniform covariate partition, the sharp absolute-cost COT lower endpoint is \(L_K=a-b\rho_K\), where \(\rho_K\) is the realized correlation of two deterministic sign arrays. When \(\lambda_K=n_0n_1/K\) remains finite and triple collisions vanish, a Poisson number of cross-arm collisions carries the minimax information: parameter-free supported-mixture kernels and a uniform deterministic-array approximation yield exact minimax absolute-risk and honest-length transfer, with shrinking rational interval-action certificates and explicit tail, off-grid coverage, and rounding errors. When \(\lambda_K\) diverges sparsely, the unprojected estimator is uniformly studentized Gaussian and the deterministic-shell local minimax theorem gives the matching interior variance frontier. Embedding cell \(j\) as \(j/K\) transfers the finite frontiers and, through pointwise shell inclusion followed by the ordered lower limits, the local variance as converse lower bounds to every anchor-admissible containing class. No broader-class upper bound is claimed; continuous achievability remains confined to the declared growing-roughness interpolation image.

project_justification.gap: The closest cited identification anchor, Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn (2026, Theorem~1), supplies general sharp conditional-transport identification under compact-domain and continuous-cost conditions, but not the collision experiment or a local minimax calculation. Hirano and Porter (2003, Theorem~3) supplies a standard LAN and local-efficiency template. Neither result establishes the matching ordered local-minimax lower and upper bounds for the deterministic-shell binary uniform-cell submodel, the finite marked-Poisson honest-length frontier, or converse transfer to arbitrary containing anchor classes.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a collision-indexed information frontier: exact finite-information decisions when \(\lambda_K\) is bounded, Gaussian local efficiency when it diverges sparsely, and a precise separation between a matching theorem on the deterministic-shell submodel and converse-only implications for broader COT classes.
project_justification.fill: The project proves a marked-Poisson reduction with parameter-free forward and reverse randomization under shell-conditioned legal mixtures, uniform collision approximation for every deterministic array, and exact rational interval certificates on the admissible domain \(m+1>\lambda_s^+\). It also derives the marked likelihood and newly closes the ordered bounded-truncated-quadratic local-minimax lower and upper bounds on the deterministic-shell binary uniform-cell submodel. Embedding transfers these results upward only as converse lower bounds to containing anchor classes; no collision-based upper bound or equality is claimed there.

body.related_work: Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn (2026, AISTATS, Theorems~1--6) establish general sharp COT bounds, continuity, and statistical guarantees. Their Theorem~1 is the closest identification anchor: it supplies sharp identification under a compact covariate domain, compact convex ambient outcome domain, overlap, and a continuous objective. The affine binary endpoint and every collision claim here are separately proved, and alternating embedded signs need not satisfy their later uniform smoothness or rate hypotheses. Hirano and Porter (2003, Theorem~3) provide the closest standard LAN and local asymptotic efficiency ingredient; what is inherited is the limit-experiment template, not the present likelihood calculation or transfer. The deterministic-shell theorem newly proves the matching ordered bounded-truncated-quadratic local-minimax lower and upper bounds only for the binary uniform-cell shells. Its extension to a full anchor-containing class is converse-only by submodel monotonicity. Ji, Lei, and Spector (2023, Theorems~3.1--3.5) provide model-agnostic dual inference and emphasize binning loss, but do not optimize honest expected length or identify this collision frontier. Ober-Reynolds (2023) derives sharp OT intervals and root-\(n\) inference in an instrumental-variables noncompliance model, not sparse covariate collisions. Paninski (2008) and Kipnis (2026) show that collisions govern sparse large-alphabet testing; Kipnis's supported-mixture architecture is especially close, but concerns one-sample uniformity testing. Arratia, Goldstein, and Gordon (1989, Theorem~1) supply dependency-neighborhood Poisson approximation. Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005, Theorem~1 and Corollary~1) and Stoye (2009, Propositions~1--2) inform confidence-set duality and boundary repair, but do not supply the admissible tail truncation, likelihood modulus, endpoint expansion, or exact rational verification here. Low and Zhou (2007) and Armstrong and Koles\'ar (2021) motivate the restricted pushforward and bias-aware scope, without supporting an upper claim over a full smoothness ball.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The former two-fixed-array lower witness is invalid because armwise marginal imbalance reveals the endpoint without cross-arm collisions. Every lower bound therefore uses mixtures supported on legal arrays and pays the discrepancy between the mixture index and the realized \(L_K\). The displayed Poisson-tail Chernoff certificate is valid only on the declared domain \(m+1>\lambda_s^+\); no arbitrary-truncation certificate is claimed. Floating-point linear-program output may only propose a basis: a certificate exists only after every likelihood, tail, action-length, primal, and dual quantity is outward-rounded and the rational inequalities are checked exactly. Endpoint decisions may be clipped to \(\mathcal D\) without increasing absolute or squared loss, but projection of \(\widehat L_K\) onto the narrower \(\mathcal A\) is excluded from the local Gaussian theorem because it changes boundary risk. The broader local classes need not be nested in \(H\), so their transfer uses \(\liminf_{H\to\infty}\), not an asserted limit.
body.honest_scope: The finite-\(\lambda\) comparison and decision theorems concern the realized endpoint \(L_K\) over the full legal deterministic-array class. Rational interval certificates require computable inputs, the admissibility condition \(m+1>\lambda_s^+\), and exact outward-rounded likelihood, tail, action-length, primal, and dual checks; floating-point output alone is not a certificate. The sparse theorem gives unprojected studentized Gaussian inference, while the matching ordered local-minimax variance theorem is confined to interior deterministic shells in the binary uniform-cell submodel. Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn's Theorem~1 supplies the closest general identification anchor, and Hirano and Porter's Theorem~3 supplies a standard LAN template; neither supplies the shell theorem proved here. Embedded finite-array laws meet the anchor's compact-covariate, compact-convex-outcome, continuous-cost conditions, so global and local results transfer to every containing class only as converse lower bounds. There is no broader-class collision upper bound or equality. Continuous achievability transfers only through the declared interpolation-image kernels; no raw total-variation comparison is asserted between continuous covariates and discrete labels. No claim covers unknown amplitudes, nonuniform cells, nonnegligible triple collisions, or a full continuous smoothness class. Coarsening changes the endpoint unless a separate bias theorem is supplied.
